statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer n (pc(0)=0). The function returns a result r, and r = sum_{i : 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) = k} nums[i]. If no index i satisfies the condition, r is the empty sum 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not panic, fail, or overflow).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n (pc(0)=0). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no index i such that 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) = k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n (pc(0)=0). If k = 0, then the function returns a result r with r = nums[0].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n. Since len(nums) <= 1000, every index i satisfies 0 <= i <= 999; the smallest nonnegative integer with 10 set bits is 1023, so no index has pc(i) >= 10. Therefore if k = 10, the function returns a result r with r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n. For every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) = k, the function returns a result r with r >= nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n. For every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) != k, whenever the function returns a result r, r + nums[i] <= sum_{j=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n. For every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) != k, and every integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000, let nums' be the slice of the same length such that nums'[i] = v and nums'[j] = nums[j] for all j != i. The function returns the same result on (nums, k) and on (nums', k): there exist r and r' such that the call on (nums, k) returns r, the call on (nums', k) returns r', and r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums), 1 <= nums[j] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.

statement: Let pc(n) denote the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of n. Whenever the function returns a result r, r + sum_{i : 0 <= i < len(nums) and pc(i) != k} nums[i] = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; and 0 <= k <= 10.
